description: Registry of known divergences between AS2 implementation and book methodology

divergences.title: r* uses total K instead of productive K*
divergences.description: The Marxian profit rate r* = S*/(C*+V*) should use capital stock restricted to productive sectors (K*). Current implementation uses total private fixed assets K from BEA Fixed Assets Table 4.1, which includes unproductive sector capital. This overstates the denominator and understates r*.
divergences.book_methodology: Shaikh & Tonak restrict K to productive sectors using IO-based classification (Ch 4). The productive capital stock K* excludes FIRE, government, and other unproductive sector fixed assets.
divergences.current_implementation: Uses total K from BEA Fixed Assets because sector-level restriction requires the IO classification from Chapter 4 (Wave 2).
divergences.impact: r* level is lower than book values; trend direction is preserved
divergences.resolution_plan: After Wave 2 (IO chapter), apply sector classification to restrict K to productive sectors. Cross-validate with Mohun (2005) capital stock estimates.
divergences.resolution_actual: M02_adjust_profit_rates.py excludes financial-sector capital (BEA Table 4.1 Line 33). K* = Total - Financial, increasing r* by 2.5-7.9% (avg +5.7%). First approximation; full industry-level restriction requires detailed Fixed Assets data.

divergences.title: VA*/W = 1.238 constant assumption in Phase 3
divergences.description: Phase 3 of the Shaikh Tonak project assumed VA*/W (value added per worker in productive vs all sectors) is approximately constant at 1.238 across the entire 1948-1989 period. This simplification was used to derive V* from total compensation W. The book's actual methodology computes V*/W from the ec_u/ec_p ratio (employee compensation per worker in unproductive vs productive sectors).
divergences.book_methodology: V*/W = (Lp/L) × (ec_u/ec_p). The book shows ec_u/ec_p ≈ 1 empirically, making V*/W ≈ Lp/L. But this ratio varies slightly across years.
divergences.current_implementation: Phase 3 used a constant VA*/W = 1.238, which produces exploitation rates that match book benchmarks (1948: 1.70, 1989: 2.44) but may diverge at non-benchmark years.
divergences.impact: Inter-benchmark year values may differ from true book values by small amounts. Benchmark years match by construction.
divergences.resolution_plan: Replace constant with year-varying ec_u/ec_p ratio computed from actual BLS CES data. Validate that benchmark years still match within 0.1%.
divergences.resolution_progress: 2026-03-30: compute_exploitation_from_wage_share() updated to accept year-varying pd.Series for va_star_over_w (backward-compatible). Full resolution requires regenerating T506_ext_parsed.csv from T512 and year-varying VA*/W series instead of using the pre-spliced data from the Shaikh Tonak project. The pre-spliced data has the constant 1.238 baked in. For 1990-1997, industry-level compensation data is unavailable via BEA API (SIC-era gap), so interpolation or constant assumption is still needed for that bridge period.
